sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Sahuarita, Arizona?
sections.html:
You can sell through an agent listing, on your own, or to a cash buyer who skips the mortgage. The right choice depends on how soon you need to close and how much work the house needs. Sahuarita is a town of owner-occupied family homes, with 81.0 percent of occupied homes lived in by their owners.

  • Agent listing: you prepare the house, allow showings and wait for the buyer's loan to clear.
  • Sale by owner: you set the price, meet buyers and prepare the deed and affidavit yourself.
  • Cash sale: the buyer pays without a bank, and you weigh the offer against the net from a listing after repairs and fees.

Whatever you choose, get the terms in writing and check the code and permit points further down before you sign.

sections.h2: Where is Sahuarita and how did it start?
sections.html:
Sahuarita is a town in Pima County, 15 miles south of Tucson and just north of Green Valley, at an elevation of 2,703 feet. Its ZIP code is 85629. The area was settled in 1911 and the town incorporated in 1994. Sahuarita operates under a council-manager form of government and is a general law town, so it has no town charter and works under Title 9 of the Arizona Revised Statutes.

The Santa Cruz River runs through the town and flows mostly during monsoon storms or long wet periods, and Madera Canyon, a bird-watching destination, lies just southeast. James Kilroy Brown created Sahuarita Ranch in 1879 and chose the name because of the saguaros in the area. The Continental Farm, founded in 1915 along the Santa Cruz River, passed to Farmers Investment Co. in 1948, which switched to pecans in 1965. The Wikipedia entry for Sahuarita describes the orchard as more than 6,000 acres. The Titan Missile Museum, built in 1963, is open to visitors.

The town grew from 3,242 residents in 2000 to 25,259 in 2010 and 34,134 in 2020. The Census Bureau estimates 37,694 as of July 1, 2025, which is 10.6 percent above the 2020 estimates base. The Census QuickFacts numbers below show a younger, higher-income town than Prescott or Prescott Valley.

sections.h2: Which Sahuarita neighborhoods do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Buyers usually ask about the master planned communities, because their rules and fees differ from a standard subdivision. Sahuarita contains Rancho Sahuarita and its resort in the north, Quail Creek in the southeast and Madera Highlands in the south. Older residential areas include La Joya in the southwest, Valle Verde del Norte, established in 1979, and Los Colonias and Los Arroyos in the west.

Rancho Sahuarita also holds Sahuarita Lake, a managed lake completed on June 22, 2001, with a one-mile perimeter and a maximum depth of 10 feet. If your house sits in one of the planned communities, request the association's governing documents and a statement of dues from the association, since the buyer will ask for both during escrow.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers near Sahuarita?
sections.html:
The school district tops the list, followed by a retirement community, big retailers and the mine. According to the town's 2024 annual financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia, the principal employers are Sahuarita Unified School District (805 employees), La Posada (472), Walmart (364), Fry's Food and Drug (271), the Town of Sahuarita (198) and Northwest Medical Center (166). The Asarco Mission Complex mine is also in Sahuarita and is described as one of its largest employers.

The mean commute is 28.6 minutes. The Sun Shuttle serves Sahuarita and Tucson on weekdays only, so a buyer who works in Tucson will weigh the drive. A buyer comparing Sahuarita with Tucson neighborhoods will ask about that drive.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Sahuarita homes?
sections.html:
Most of the town is in Sahuarita Unified School District, and a portion is in the Continental Elementary School District. Because boundaries do not follow the town line, ask the district to confirm the assigned schools for your exact address before you advertise them.

School assignment is one of the first things a family buyer checks. If you know the district for your street, put it in the listing or the offer packet so buyers do not have to chase it.

sections.h2: Which Sahuarita permit and code rules can affect a sale?
sections.html:
Unpermitted work and open complaints are the two items that most often surface in an inspection. The Community Development Department handles building and zoning compliance. According to the town's code enforcement page, weeds, junk vehicles and illegal signs go to Planning and Zoning, while a structure built without a permit and a substandard or dangerous structure go to Building Safety. Complaints can be filed through the Accela Citizen Access portal, in person, or by phone at (520) 822-8852.

Under the town's building permit guidance, most alterations, replacements and repairs need a permit. A few small items do not, and the list includes the following.

  • A one-story detached shed up to 200 square feet with no plumbing, electrical or mechanical work.
  • Masonry walls up to 6 feet high, and wood, vinyl or wrought iron fences up to 7 feet.
  • Retaining walls not over 4 feet high, and private concrete paths and driveways.
  • Painting, tile, carpet and cabinet replacement.
  • Decks up to 200 square feet and no more than 30 inches above grade that are not attached to the house.

Anything larger, such as a room addition, a patio enclosure or new wiring, belongs with the Building Safety Division at 520-822-8866. If you added something without a permit, call before you list so you can decide whether to permit it or to disclose it and sell as is.

sections.h2: How is a Sahuarita sale recorded in Pima County?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Pima County Recorder, which charges a flat $30 for recording any document under A.R.S. 11-475, according to the Pima County Recorder fee page. Returning a document submitted in error costs $5, and mailed documents carry a $1 processing fee. The recorder takes cash, checks and money orders, and accepts Visa and Mastercard only for in-person payments, and the affidavit of property value form comes from the Arizona Department of Revenue.

Under A.R.S. 11-1133, a deed that transfers title must carry that affidavit, signed by the buyer and seller or their agents, and the recorder must refuse the deed without a complete affidavit unless it has an exemption notation. The form asks for the price, the parcel number and the date of sale. Ask the Pima County Treasurer for the current tax bill, since the closing figures depend on it.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Pima County?
faqs.a: The Pima County Recorder charges a flat $30 to record any document. There is an extra $1 mail processing fee per document if you send it by mail. The affidavit of property value form is available from the Arizona Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a shed or fence in Sahuarita?
faqs.a: Not always. The town lists a one-story detached shed up to 200 square feet with no utilities, masonry walls up to 6 feet and fences up to 7 feet as exempt from a building permit. Anything larger, or with plumbing or electrical work, needs a permit. Some projects still need a zoning clearance.
Most of the town is in Sahuarita Unified School District, and a portion is in the Continental Elementary School District. Confirm the assignment for your address with the district.

faqs.q: How many people live in Sahuarita?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 37,694 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 34,134 and the 2010 census counted 25,259. Median household income was $104,680 for 2020 to 2024.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a code complaint in Sahuarita?
faqs.a: Call the Community Development Department at (520) 822-8852, file online through Accela Citizen Access, or visit in person. For permit questions, the Building Safety Division is at 520-822-8866.
